Threat.value: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place

The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to
Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory

vignette:
Asad was a 78-year-old roofer with a weathered face that spoke of years spent under the sun, his hands roughened by labor. He had spent his life working hard to provide for his family and had found joy in the simple pleasures of life, like watching his grandchildren play. However, a traumatic event from three years ago had changed everything. It was a day like any other when he was called to a roofing job at an old industrial building. Asad had been working alongside his younger colleagues when a sudden chemical spill occurred, releasing noxious fumes into the air. The potent odor enveloped them, and in a matter of moments, Asad felt dizzy and disoriented. He remembered gasping for air, stumbling as he tried to escape the cloud of toxic chemicals. The experience left him shaken; he had never felt so vulnerable, so helpless.

In the months that followed, Asad's life transformed in ways he could never have anticipated. The vivid memories of that day haunted him, creeping into his mind during quiet moments, forcing their way to the surface when he least expected it. He often found himself sitting in his living room, unable to relax even in the comfort of his own home. The once peaceful space felt stifling, and he could not shake the feeling that danger lurked just out of sight. What frightened him most was the unpredictable nature of it all; he had come to believe that he could no longer trust his own instincts.

Asad started to notice that he would react with alarm whenever someone touched him unexpectedly. A gentle hand on his shoulder from his wife, Leila, would send his heart racing, and he would flinch away instinctively. She would look at him with concern, her brow furrowing as she said, "Asad, it's just me." But the reassurance did little to soothe his frayed nerves. He felt burdened by the thought that he could no longer enjoy simple physical affection, something he had cherished in their long marriage.

The evenings were particularly difficult. Sleep eluded him as he lay in bed, replaying the events of that day in his mind. He would toss and turn, often waking in a panic, drenched in sweat, unable to grasp the specifics of the memories that haunted him. It wasn't just the memory of the spill that tormented him; sometimes, the emotional weight of the experience enveloped him without a clear image or recollection of the event. It felt as though the feelings existed in a vacuum, overwhelming him despite the absence of tangible memories. This confusion left him frustrated, as he struggled to articulate what he felt to Leila, who tried to comfort him but could not fully understand his internal turmoil.

Asad's avoidance behaviors began to take shape over time. He started to withdraw from family gatherings, especially those involving children. Being around his grandchildren, once a source of joy, now felt unbearable. He feared that if he lost control, he might react inappropriately or, worse, expose them to his anxieties. Even watching the news became a ritual he avoided, as stories of environmental disasters and chemical spills would flood him with dread. He would sit in silence when news reports came on, his heart racing with an urgency to change the channel, as if by avoiding the content, he could shield himself from the associated memories.

Asad's world became smaller, and his relationships began to suffer. Friends would call, inviting him out, but he would find excuses, preferring the safety of solitude. After a while, he noticed Leila's disappointment, her eyes occasionally betraying her worry. Asad felt isolated, trapped in a cycle of avoidance that he could not seem to break. It wasn't just the fear of the past that plagued him; it was the fear of losing the life he had built, the connections he had nurtured.

It was during a quiet evening, while watching a home video of his grandchildren, that he felt a deep pang of longing and sadness. The laughter and joy of the children contrasted sharply with his own internal struggle, and it struck him that he had to seek help. He realized that he could not continue living in fear, unable to enjoy the moments that mattered most. Asad decided it was time to confront the shadows of his past, hoping to reclaim the joy of being present with his family. As he sat in the therapist's office, he felt a mix of apprehension and hope, wondering if he could find a way to heal and reconnect with the life he once loved so deeply.
